answer.reason: The Dominican Republic has a relatively young population; its share of residents aged 65 and above has been gradually rising from around 6% in 2010 to roughly 7.5–8% by 2023. A value of about 7.58% is consistent with this trajectory, whereas 11.24% would be far too high for the Dominican Republic in 2023 (that range is more typical of countries with substantially older populations). Therefore option B is the supported answer.
